title: Students and trade unionists protest school conditions in Paris
seoTitle: Paris student protests over school conditions

tea.why: Students are protesting against overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, deteriorating school infrastructure, and stressful admissions processes.
tea.want: Protesters demand better-resourced schools, improved facilities, and government action to address educational inequality.
tea.changed: Oct 13: The Interior Ministry reported 161,500 demonstrators nationwide, while unions estimated participation at nearly 480,000.

summary: Since mid-September 2026, students in Paris and across France have engaged in blockades and marches to protest deteriorating school conditions. Organised by student groups and supported by trade unions, the movement highlights issues such as overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, and inadequate infrastructure. Protesters also express frustration with the Parcoursup university admissions system. The demonstrations have faced a significant police response, leading to thousands of arrests and reports of injuries among students, staff, and officers. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has accused the La France Insoumise party of exploiting the movement for electoral gain, while protesters argue that the government has failed to address systemic educational inequality. Further demonstrations involving various groups are expected to continue, with tensions persisting between demonstrators and security forces.
response: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused the radical-left of instrumentalising the movement. Authorities have deployed large security forces, resulting in mass arrests and the suspension of certain riot-control weapons following reports of severe injuries.

arrests.text: Justice Ministry figures cited in reports put the number of people taken into custody at roughly 6,800 to 8,000.

injuries.text: The government reported more than 900 officers and more than 150 teachers and school staffers have been injured.

updates.text: Protests began with high school blockades in the Paris region, particularly around Creteil.
Large-scale demonstrations occurred nationwide with turnout estimates ranging from 161,500 to 480,000.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu accused the La France Insoumise party of exploiting the student movement for electoral advantage.
